ACC-001.q: Match each type of accounting record with its minimum retention period:
p: Documents not used directly for bookkeeping, used for management
Documents used directly for bookkeeping, ledgers, annual financial statements
Records of historical significance or importance to economy, security, defence
ACC-001.e: Under the 2015 Accounting Law and Decree 174/2016/ND-CP.
ACC-001.x:
Basis: Article 41 of Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13; Decree 174/2016/ND-CP.
Analysis: Minimum retention: documents not used directly for posting (management use) – 5 years; posting vouchers, ledgers, annual FS – 10 years; historically significant records – permanently.
Note: E-invoices used for posting fall in the 10-year group (ADM-044).

ACC-002.q: The required practical accounting experience to be appointed chief accountant is:
o: At least 2 years with a university degree or higher; at least 3 years with intermediate/college level (plus a chief accountant training certificate)
At least 5 years for all levels
No experience required with a certificate
ACC-002.e: Article 54 of the 2015 Accounting Law; also requires accounting qualifications from intermediate level and a chief accountant certificate.
ACC-002.x:
Basis: Article 54 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
Analysis: A chief accountant needs: accounting qualification at intermediate level or above; a chief accountant training certificate; at least 2 years' practical experience (university) or 3 years (intermediate/college).
Distractors: B, C and D don't match the statutory conditions.

ACC-003.q: Cashiers, storekeepers and persons buying/selling assets may not concurrently act as accountants in the same accounting unit (except sole proprietorships, single-member LLCs owned by an individual and cases prescribed by the Government).
ACC-003.e: True under Article 52 of the 2015 Accounting Law — a basic segregation-of-duties principle.
ACC-003.x:
Basis: Article 52 of the 2015 Accounting Law; COSO 2013 (segregation of duties).
Analysis: True. Cashiers, storekeepers and buyers/sellers of assets may not also be accountants – separating custody from recording so one person can't both misappropriate and conceal. Exceptions: sole proprietorships, single-owner LLCs and Government-specified cases.

ACC-004.q: The first or final annual accounting period may be shorter or longer than 12 months but must not exceed:
ACC-004.x:
Basis: Article 12 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
Analysis: The first or last annual period may be shorter or longer than 12 months but not over 15 – mirroring the CIT first-year combination rule (CIT-009).
Distractors: 18, 13 and 24 months are wrong.

ACC-005.q: The accounting currency is the Vietnamese dong; enterprises transacting mainly in foreign currency may choose it as the accounting currency but must translate financial statements used in Vietnam into VND.
ACC-005.e: True under Article 10 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
ACC-005.x:
Basis: Article 10 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
Analysis: True. The accounting currency is VND; businesses transacting mainly in foreign currency may choose it, but FS used in Vietnam must be translated into VND (ACC-020).

ACC-006.q: Micro enterprises may assign a person in charge of accounting without appointing a chief accountant.
ACC-006.e: True. They may also hire accounting or chief-accountant services.
ACC-006.x:
Basis: 2015 Accounting Law; Decree 174/2016/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Micro-enterprises may appoint a person in charge of accounting instead of a chief accountant, or outsource – easing compliance for small firms.

ACC-007.q: Enterprises may hire accounting service firms to do bookkeeping or act as chief accountant.
ACC-007.e: True under Article 56 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
ACC-007.x:
Basis: Article 56 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
Analysis: True. Businesses may hire accounting service firms for bookkeeping or as chief accountant; hirees must meet the standards. Ultimate responsibility for the FS stays with the legal representative.

ACC-008.q: Electronic documents complying with the law are accounting documents with the same value as paper ones.
ACC-008.e: True under Articles 17 and 18 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
ACC-008.x:
Basis: Articles 17 and 18 of the 2015 Accounting Law; 2023 E-Transactions Law.
Analysis: True. Electronic vouchers meeting requirements (content, e-signature, integrity, retrievability) are as valid as paper.

ACC-009.q: Select ALL methods for correcting accounting records when errors are found:
o: Correction method (strike through once and write the correct figure)
Tearing out the page with the error
ACC-009.e: Erasing or destroying pages is prohibited; electronic ledgers use negative or supplementary entries.
ACC-009.x:
Basis: Article 27 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
Analysis: Three correction methods: (A) striking through once and writing the right figure (paper books, before totals); (B) negative (red) entries reversing the error; (C) supplementary entries for omissions.
Distractors: (D) erasing and (E) tearing pages are prohibited. Electronic ledgers use only negative or supplementary entries, leaving an audit trail.

ACC-010.q: Annual financial statements of foreign-invested enterprises must be audited.
ACC-010.e: True under the law on independent audit; certain others (public companies, credit institutions…) are also mandatory.
ACC-010.x:
Basis: Independent Audit Law 67/2011/QH12; Decree 17/2012/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. FDI enterprises' annual FS must be audited; other mandatory groups include public companies, credit institutions, insurers and State enterprises…

ACC-011.q: The deadline for submitting annual financial statements for most enterprises (not SOEs, sole proprietorships or partnerships) is:
o: Within 90 days after the end of the annual accounting period
ACC-011.e: Sole proprietorships and partnerships: within 30 days.
ACC-011.x:
Basis: Accounting Law 2015; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Most enterprises file annual FS within 90 days of year-end (matching the CIT deadline); sole proprietorships and partnerships within 30 days.
Distractors: 30 days is for proprietorships and partnerships only; 45 and 120 days don't apply.

ACC-012.q: Enterprises must close their books at period-end before preparing financial statements and in other prescribed cases.
ACC-012.e: True under Article 26 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
ACC-012.x:
Basis: Article 26 of the 2015 Accounting Law.
Analysis: True. Books are closed at period-end before FS preparation and on stock-takes, mergers, splits, dissolutions… – ensuring figures don't change after reporting.

ACC-013.q: Accounting records past their retention period are destroyed by decision of the legal representative, with a destruction committee and minutes.
ACC-013.e: True. No destruction before the period ends or without the procedure.
ACC-013.x:
Basis: Accounting Law 2015; Decree 174/2016/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Records past retention are destroyed by decision of the legal representative, with a destruction committee and minutes. Early or undocumented destruction is a violation and risky at audit.

ACC-014.q: The enterprise accounting regime under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC takes effect from:
ACC-014.e: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC was issued on 27/10/2025 and applies to financial years starting from 01/01/2026.
ACC-014.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Issued 27/10/2025, applicable from financial years starting 01/01/2026, replacing Circular 200/2014.
Distractors: B is the issue date; C and D are wrong.

ACC-015.q: Under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC, the 'Balance Sheet' is renamed the 'Statement of Financial Position'.
ACC-015.x:
Basis: Article 17 of Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. The 'Balance Sheet' is renamed the 'Statement of Financial Position', aligning with IFRS terminology.

ACC-016.q: Match the sub-accounts of account 215 – Biological assets (Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC) with their content:
p: Livestock yielding periodic produce (e.g., dairy cows)
Livestock yielding produce once (e.g., beef cattle)
Seasonal crops or crops harvested once
ACC-016.e: Account 215 is new and especially important for livestock and crop enterprises.
ACC-016.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Account 215 – Biological assets (new): 2151 – animals producing periodically (dairy cows, laying hens); 2152 – animals for one-off produce (beef cattle, pigs); 2153 – seasonal or one-harvest crops. It separates biological assets from inventory and ordinary fixed assets – closer to IAS 41.

ACC-017.q: Match the account number with its new name under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC:
ACC-017.e: Under Circular 200: 112 Cash in bank; 155 Finished goods; 242 Prepaid expenses; 419 Treasury shares.
ACC-017.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (versus Circular 200/2014).
Analysis: New names: 112 – Demand deposits (was Bank deposits); 155 – Products (was Finished goods); 242 – Deferred costs (was Prepaid expenses); 419 – Own shares repurchased (was Treasury shares).

ACC-018.q: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC requires enterprises to develop internal governance regulations (or equivalent documents) and organise internal control.
ACC-018.e: True under Article 3(2) of Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC — new compared with Circular 200.
ACC-018.x:
Basis: Article 3(2) of Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. New: businesses must set internal governance rules and organise internal control – linking governance to accounting quality, consistent with COSO.

ACC-019.q: Under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC, enterprises that design or amend document/ledger forms or accounts, or add financial statement items, must issue an accounting regulation but do not need MOF approval.
ACC-019.e: True. Under Circular 200, changes to accounts or report items required MOF approval.
ACC-019.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Businesses may design or modify vouchers, books, accounts and add FS line items by issuing accounting rules – no Ministry approval as under Circular 200. In return they bear responsibility for appropriateness.

ACC-020.q: Under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC, when translating foreign-currency financial statements into VND, assets and liabilities are translated at:
o: The average transfer buying/selling rate of the commercial bank the enterprise regularly uses at period-end
The rate at the capital contribution date
The SBV central rate at the beginning of the year
ACC-020.e: Contributed capital uses the actual rate at contribution; income statement and cash flow items use actual or period-average rates (within tolerance).
ACC-020.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Translating foreign-currency FS into VND: assets and liabilities at the average transfer buy/sell rate of the main bank at period-end; contributed capital at the contribution-date rate; income and cash flow items at actual or period-average rates.
Distractors: B applies to capital; C to income items; D is wrong.

ACC-021.q: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC adds sub-account 82112 to record top-up CIT expense under global minimum tax rules.
ACC-021.e: True. It applies to constituent entities of MNE groups within the scope of Resolution 107/2023/QH15.
ACC-021.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; Resolution 107/2023/QH15.
Analysis: True. Account 82112 records top-up CIT under the global minimum tax for in-scope MNE constituent entities (FCT-084).

ACC-022.q: How many basic accounting principles does VAS 01 – Framework set out?
ACC-022.e: Accrual basis, going concern, historical cost, matching, consistency, prudence, materiality.
ACC-022.x:
Basis: VAS 01 – Framework.
Analysis: VAS 01 sets 7 basic principles: accruals, going concern, historical cost, matching, consistency, prudence, materiality.
Distractors: 5, 10 and 12 are wrong.

ACC-023.q: Select ALL basic accounting principles under VAS 01:
o: Recognising revenue when cash is received
Measuring all assets at fair value
ACC-023.e: The other two are Matching and Materiality. Cash-based revenue recognition contradicts the accrual basis.
ACC-023.x:
Basis: VAS 01.
Analysis: Correct: (A) accruals; (B) going concern; (C) historical cost; (D) consistency; (E) prudence (plus matching and materiality).
Distractors: (F) cash-basis revenue contradicts accruals; (G) VAS is cost-based, not fair value for all assets (unlike IFRS for some items).

ACC-024.q: Match each accounting principle with its content:
p: Record transactions when they occur, not when cash is received or paid
Revenue and related expenses are recognised in the same period
Do not overstate assets/income or understate liabilities/expenses
Information whose omission or misstatement could significantly distort the statements and affect users' decisions
ACC-024.x:
Basis: VAS 01.
Analysis: Accruals – record when transactions occur, not on cash. Matching – related revenue and costs in the same period. Prudence – don't overstate assets or income, or understate liabilities or expenses. Materiality – information whose omission or misstatement could influence users' decisions.

ACC-025.q: Select ALL conditions for recognising revenue from sales of goods under VAS 14:
o: Significant risks and rewards of ownership have been transferred to the buyer
The seller retains neither managerial involvement nor control over the goods
Economic benefits have flowed or will flow from the transaction
Costs related to the transaction can be measured
ACC-025.e: The five conditions of VAS 14; cash collection is not a condition.
ACC-025.x:
Basis: VAS 14 – Revenue and other income.
Analysis: Five conditions for sales revenue: (A) significant risks and rewards transferred; (B) no continuing management or control; (C) revenue measurable reliably; (D) economic benefits probable; (E) related costs measurable.
Distractors: (F) Cash receipt isn't a condition (accruals).

ACC-026.q: Select ALL items included in the cost of inventories under VAS 02:
o: Transport and handling costs during purchase
ACC-026.e: Selling, administration expenses and abnormal wastage are expensed in the period.
ACC-026.x:
Basis: VAS 02 – Inventories.
Analysis: Cost includes (A) purchase price and non-refundable taxes; (B) inbound freight and handling; (C) conversion costs (direct labour, production overheads).
Distractors: (D) selling costs, (E) administrative costs and (F) abnormal wastage are period expenses – not capitalised.

ACC-027.q: Select ALL inventory costing methods allowed under the current regime:
ACC-027.e: LIFO has not been permitted since Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC.
ACC-027.x:
Basis: VAS 02; Circulars 200/2014 and 99/2025.
Analysis: Permitted costing methods: (A) specific identification; (B) weighted average; (C) FIFO.
Distractors: (D) LIFO has been disallowed since Circular 200/2014 (also banned by IFRS) as it distorts inventory values when prices change.

ACC-028.q: Opening stock is 1,000 kg of steel sheet at VND 20,000/kg; purchases 3,000 kg at VND 24,000/kg. Issued 2,500 kg. Under periodic weighted average, what is the value issued (VND)?
ACC-028.e: Average cost = (20 + 72) million / 4,000 kg = 23,000 VND/kg. Value issued = 2,500 × 23,000 = 57,500,000 VND.
ACC-028.x:
Basis: VAS 02.
Working: Total value = 1,000 × 20,000 + 3,000 × 24,000 = 20 + 72 = 92 million; 4,000 kg → average 23,000 VND/kg. Issue 2,500 kg × 23,000 = 57,500,000 VND; closing 1,500 kg × 23,000 = 34.5 million.
Note: FIFO would give 1,000 × 20,000 + 1,500 × 24,000 = 56 million.

ACC-029.q: Under VAS 02, inventories are measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
ACC-029.e: True. The difference is recognised as an inventory write-down provision.
ACC-029.x:
Basis: VAS 02; Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Inventory is carried at the lower of cost and net realisable value (estimated selling price − costs to complete and sell); the shortfall is a write-down allowance (account 2294) – applying prudence.

ACC-030.q: Under VAS 16, borrowing costs are capitalised into an asset when:
o: Directly attributable to constructing or producing a qualifying asset that takes a substantial period (over 12 months) to get ready for use or sale
ACC-030.e: Otherwise borrowing costs are recognised as financial expenses in the period.
ACC-030.x:
Basis: VAS 16 – Borrowing costs.
Analysis: Borrowing costs are capitalised when directly attributable to constructing or producing qualifying assets needing a substantial period (over 12 months) to be ready; otherwise expensed.
Distractors: B, C and D wrongly widen capitalisation.

ACC-031.q: Under VAS 17, a taxable temporary difference (carrying amount of an asset greater than its tax base) gives rise to:
ACC-031.e: For example, book depreciation lower than tax-deductible depreciation.
ACC-031.x:
Basis: VAS 17 – Income taxes.
Analysis: Carrying amount > tax base → recovery will yield more taxable income than accounting profit → a taxable temporary difference → deferred tax liability (CIT-136). E.g., faster tax depreciation.
Distractors: B is for deductible differences; C and D are different concepts.

ACC-032.q: At end-2026, taxable temporary differences are VND 500 million; CIT rate 20%. What deferred tax liability should be recognised (VND)?
ACC-032.x:
Basis: VAS 17; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Working: Deferred tax liability = 500,000,000 × 20% = 100,000,000 VND: Dr 8212 / Cr 347.
Note: Use the rate expected when the difference reverses (possibly 15%/17% for small firms).

ACC-033.q: Select ALL conditions for recognising a provision under VAS 18:
o: A present obligation (legal or constructive) arising from a past event
A probable outflow of economic benefits to settle the obligation
A reliable estimate of the obligation can be made
ACC-033.e: VAS 18 does not allow provisions for future operating losses.
ACC-033.x:
Basis: VAS 18 – Provisions, contingent liabilities and assets.
Analysis: A provision is recognised when: (A) a present obligation (legal or constructive) arises from a past event; (B) an outflow of benefits is probable; (C) a reliable estimate exists.
Distractors: (D) Future operating losses aren't present obligations – no provision.

ACC-034.q: Identify which events after the annual reporting date are ADJUSTING events under VAS 23 (True = adjusting):
o: A court ruling after closing confirms an obligation that existed at 31/12
A fire destroys a warehouse on 15/01 of the following year
A major customer goes bankrupt after closing; the receivable existed at 31/12
A share issue to increase capital in February of the following year
ACC-034.e: Events providing evidence of conditions existing at the reporting date are adjusting; new events are only disclosed.
ACC-034.x:
Basis: VAS 23 – Events after the reporting period.
Analysis: Adjusting: (1) a judgment confirming an obligation existing at 31/12; (3) a customer's bankruptcy showing the 31/12 receivable was impaired. Non-adjusting (disclose only): (2) a fire on 15/01 – a new event; (4) a share issue in February.

ACC-035.q: Match each cash flow with its activity in the cash flow statement (VAS 24, non-financial entity):
p: Cash paid to buy fixed assets
Cash paid to suppliers of goods and services
ACC-035.e: The three cash flow categories under VAS 24.
ACC-035.x:
Basis: VAS 24 – Cash flow statement.
Analysis: Fixed asset purchases – investing; dividends paid – financing; payments to suppliers – operating.

ACC-036.q: Select ALL cash flows from financing activities:
o: Proceeds from issuing shares, receiving capital contributions
Dividends and profits paid to owners
Interest received on loans, dividends received
Cash paid to buy machinery and equipment
ACC-036.e: Interest/dividends received and asset purchases are investing activities.
ACC-036.x:
Basis: VAS 24.
Analysis: Financing (changes in equity and borrowings): (A) loan proceeds; (B) loan principal repayments; (C) share issues, capital received; (D) dividends paid.
Distractors: (E) interest and dividends received and (F) machinery purchases are investing (for non-financial entities).

ACC-037.q: Operating cash flows in the cash flow statement may be prepared using:
ACC-037.e: VAS 24 allows both methods for operating cash flows.
ACC-037.x:
Basis: VAS 24.
Analysis: Operating cash flows may use the direct method (listing main receipts and payments) or indirect method (adjusting profit before tax for non-cash items and working capital). Investing and financing are direct.
Distractors: B and C are too narrow; D isn't a presentation method.

ACC-038.q: Match each change with its treatment under VAS 29:
p: Change in accounting estimate (e.g., useful life)
ACC-038.e: VAS 29 – Changes in accounting policies, estimates and errors.
ACC-038.x:
Basis: VAS 29.
Analysis: Policy changes – retrospective (restating opening balances and comparatives). Estimate changes (useful lives) – prospective, affecting current and future periods. Prior-period material errors – retrospective restatement.

ACC-039.q: Select ALL components of an enterprise's annual financial statements:
ACC-039.e: Management reports are internal and not part of the statutory financial statements.
ACC-039.x:
Basis: VAS 21; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: The annual FS set: (A) Statement of financial position; (B) Income statement; (C) Cash flow statement; (D) Notes.
Distractors: (E) Segment cost reports are internal management accounting, not statutory FS.

ACC-040.q: When the going concern assumption is no longer appropriate, financial statements must be prepared on another basis and that basis disclosed.
ACC-040.x:
Basis: VAS 01; VAS 21.
Analysis: True. When going concern no longer holds (liquidation, cessation), FS use another basis (e.g., liquidation values) with disclosure – historical cost no longer reflects recoverable value.

ACC-041.q: Exchange differences from year-end revaluation of foreign-currency monetary items (for an operating enterprise) are recognised in:
o: Financial income or financial expenses, after netting
ACC-041.e: Under VAS 10; pre-operating project exchange differences may follow specific rules.
ACC-041.x:
Basis: VAS 10 – Effects of changes in foreign exchange rates.
Analysis: For operating businesses, year-end revaluation differences on foreign-currency monetary items go to financial income (gains) or financial expenses (losses), after netting.
Distractors: B applies only to some pre-operating cases or translation; C and D are wrong.

ACC-042.q: Revenue excludes amounts collected on behalf of third parties, such as output VAT.
ACC-042.x:
Basis: VAS 14.
Analysis: True. Revenue includes only economic benefits for the entity itself; amounts collected for third parties (output VAT, pass-through collections) don't increase equity and aren't revenue.

ACC-043.q: A parent must prepare consolidated financial statements under VAS 25 (except where exempt under the standard).
ACC-043.e: True. Consolidated statements present the group as a single entity.
ACC-043.x:
Basis: VAS 25 – Consolidated FS and investments in subsidiaries.
Analysis: True. Parents prepare consolidated FS presenting the group as one entity (eliminating intra-group transactions, recognising non-controlling interests), unless exempt under the standard.

ACC-044.q: An asset is recognised as a tangible fixed asset when it simultaneously: will generate future economic benefits; has a useful life over 1 year; and has a cost:
o: Of VND 30 million or more, reliably measured
ACC-044.x:
Basis: Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC (amended by Circular 147/2016/TT-BTC).
Analysis: Three tangible fixed asset criteria: probable future benefits; useful life over 1 year; cost of at least 30 million VND, reliably measured.
Distractors: 10 million is the pre-2013 threshold; 50 and 100 million are wrong.

ACC-045.q: Assets not meeting fixed-asset criteria (cost below VND 30 million) are allocated to expenses over a maximum of 3 years.
ACC-045.x:
Basis: Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Items under 30 million (tools) aren't fixed assets; they're amortised to expense over at most 3 years (tracked in account 242 – Deferred costs under Circular 99).

ACC-046.q: A factory air-conditioning system costs VND 600 million, depreciated over 5 years straight-line. What is the annual depreciation (VND)?
ACC-046.x:
Basis: Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC (straight-line depreciation, amended by Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC); Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (enterprise accounting regime – per the question); VAS 03.
Working: Annual depreciation = cost / useful life = 600,000,000 / 5 = 120,000,000 VND/year (10,000,000 VND/month).
Analysis: The life must fall within Circular 45/2013's range for that asset group for the charge to be CIT-deductible. It goes to factory overhead because it serves the plant – flowing into product cost.
Check: 120,000,000 × 5 = 600,000,000 ✓.

ACC-047.q: Match the depreciation period with the adjustment coefficient under the adjusted declining-balance method:
ACC-047.x:
Basis: Appendix 2 of Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Adjustment factors for adjusted declining balance: up to 4 years – 1.5; over 4 to 6 years – 2.0; over 6 years – 2.5. Accelerated rate = straight-line rate × factor.

ACC-048.q: A plastic injection moulding machine costs VND 600 million, depreciated over 5 years using the adjusted declining-balance method. What is the first-year depreciation (VND)?
ACC-048.e: Straight-line rate 20% × coefficient 2.0 = 40%; first-year depreciation = 600 × 40% = 240,000,000 VND.
ACC-048.x:
Basis: Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC.
Working: Straight-line rate = 1/5 = 20%; 5 years → factor 2.0 → 40%. Year-1 depreciation = 600 × 40% = 240 million VND.
Note: In later years, switch to equal amounts when the declining figure ≤ remaining value / remaining years.

ACC-049.q: Indefinite-term land use rights are not depreciated.
ACC-049.x:
Basis: Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Indefinite land use rights have no determinable useful life, so they aren't amortised; fixed-term rights are amortised over the permitted term.

ACC-050.q: Match the overdue period of doubtful receivables with the maximum provision rate (Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC):
ACC-050.e: Provision rates for doubtful receivables by overdue period.
ACC-050.x:
Basis: Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Doubtful debt allowances by overdue period: 6 months to under 1 year – 30%; 1 to under 2 years – 50%; 2 to under 3 years – 70%; 3 years or more – 100%.

ACC-051.q: A receivable of VND 200 million from a distributor is 14 months overdue, with full documentation. What is the maximum provision (VND)?
ACC-051.x:
Basis: Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC.
Working: 14 months overdue (1 to under 2 years) → 50% × 200 = 100,000,000 VND.
Note: Contracts, confirmations and dunning records are needed; without them the allowance isn't CIT-deductible.

ACC-052.q: Raw materials are purchased into stock on credit, with deductible input VAT. The correct entry is:
ACC-052.e: Materials received: Dr 152; input VAT: Dr 1331; payable to supplier: Cr 331.
ACC-052.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Raw materials received on credit: Dr 152 (net), Dr 1331 (creditable VAT) / Cr 331 (total payable).
Distractors: B reverses it; C expenses stock directly; D uses cash although unpaid.

ACC-053.q: Finished goods are sold and the customer pays by transfer immediately. The revenue entry is:
ACC-053.e: Sales revenue Cr 511; output VAT Cr 3331.
ACC-053.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Sale by bank receipt: Dr 112 / Cr 511 (net revenue), Cr 3331 (output VAT); also Dr 632 / Cr 155 for cost.
Distractors: B reverses; C uses other income; D uses financial income.

ACC-054.q: Deducting the employee's SI share from salary. The entry is:
ACC-054.e: The employee's SI deducted from pay: Dr 334, Cr 3383.
ACC-054.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Employee social insurance deduction: Dr 334 / Cr 3383. Employer's share: Dr 622/627/641/642 / Cr 3383 (expense).
Distractors: B reverses; C is the employer's share; D is paying wages.

ACC-055.q: Recognising the year's current CIT expense payable:
ACC-055.e: At period-end, account 821 is closed to 911 to determine results.
ACC-055.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; VAS 17.
Analysis: Current CIT: Dr 8211 / Cr 3334; close 821 to 911 at period-end (CIT-118).
Distractors: B reverses; C bypasses tax expense; D misclassifies as admin expense.

ACC-056.q: Recording a provision for doubtful receivables:
ACC-056.e: Doubtful debt provision expense is recorded in general administration expenses.
ACC-056.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Doubtful debt allowance: Dr 642 / Cr 2293; reversal Dr 2293 / Cr 642.
Distractors: B is the reversal; C and D use wrong accounts.

ACC-057.q: Depreciation of factory buildings and production lines used in production:
ACC-057.e: Depreciation of production assets goes to production overheads.
ACC-057.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Production asset depreciation: Dr 627 (production overheads) / Cr 214 (accumulated depreciation), later absorbed into cost via 154.
Distractors: B reverses; C credits cost directly; D skips the overhead step.

ACC-058.q: At year-end, accruing December loan interest payable but not yet paid:
ACC-058.e: Interest expense is recognised on an accrual basis; accrued expenses are tracked in account 335.
ACC-058.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; VAS 01 (accruals).
Analysis: Accrue December interest: Dr 635 / Cr 335 (accrued expenses); on payment Dr 335 / Cr 112.
Distractors: B reverses; C credits cash before payment; D confuses it with deferred costs.

ACC-059.q: Match each account number with its name:
ACC-059.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: 131 – Receivables from customers; 331 – Payables to suppliers; 334 – Payables to employees; 421 – Undistributed profit after tax; 911 – Income summary.

ACC-060.q: Accounts in classes 5, 6, 7, 8 and account 911 have no closing balance.
ACC-060.e: True. Revenue and expense accounts are closed to 911 at period-end.
ACC-060.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Class 5–8 accounts (revenue, costs, other income/expense, tax expense) and 911 are temporary – closed to 911 then 421 at period-end, so they carry no balance.

ACC-061.q: The deadline for members, owners or shareholders to fully contribute committed capital on establishment is:
o: 90 days from the issuance of the business registration certificate
ACC-061.e: Excluding time for transporting/importing contributed assets and transferring ownership.
ACC-061.x:
Basis: Enterprise Law 59/2020/QH14 (Articles 47, 75, 113); Law 76/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Members, owners and shareholders must contribute committed capital within 90 days of registration, excluding time to transport or import contributed assets and transfer title.
Note: Interest on the unpaid portion isn't CIT-deductible (CIT-048).

ACC-062.q: Under Decree 168/2025/ND-CP, an individual is a beneficial owner of an enterprise with legal personality when they:
o: Directly or indirectly own 25% or more of charter capital, or control the enterprise
ACC-062.e: Law 76/2025/QH15 (effective 01/7/2025) adds the beneficial owner concept; Decree 168/2025/ND-CP sets the criteria.
ACC-062.x:
Basis: Law 76/2025/QH15 amending the Enterprise Law; Decree 168/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: A beneficial owner is an individual holding directly or indirectly at least 25% of charter capital, or with control (appointing most managers, deciding key matters).
Distractors: B has the wrong threshold; C and D – titles don't mean beneficial ownership.

ACC-063.q: Enterprises must collect, update and keep beneficial owner information and provide it to competent authorities on request.
ACC-063.e: True. This supports anti-money laundering and ownership transparency.
ACC-063.x:
Basis: Law 76/2025/QH15; Decree 168/2025/ND-CP; 2022 Anti-Money Laundering Law.
Analysis: True. Businesses must collect, update and keep beneficial ownership information and provide it on request – transparency, anti-money laundering, and relevance to tax related-party rules (FCT-023).

ACC-064.q: Match the phases of the IFRS adoption scheme in Vietnam (Decision 345/QĐ-BTC) with their content:
p: Mandatory adoption for certain groups of enterprises
ACC-064.x:
Basis: Decision 345/QĐ-BTC of 16/03/2020.
Analysis: IFRS roadmap: 2020–2021 preparation; 2022–2025 voluntary; after 2025 mandatory for certain groups (per Ministry rules). VFRS based on IFRS is also being developed.

ACC-065.q: A joint-stock company must pay dividends in full within:
o: 6 months from the end of the annual general meeting
ACC-065.x:
Basis: Article 135(4) of the 2020 Enterprise Law.
Analysis: Dividends must be fully paid within 6 months of the annual general meeting. They may only be paid after tax obligations, fund appropriations and covering prior losses.
Distractors: 3 and 12 months and 30 days are wrong.

ACC-066.q: An enterprise may have several legal representatives; the charter specifies their number, titles, rights and obligations.
ACC-066.e: True under Article 12 of the 2020 Enterprise Law.
ACC-066.x:
Basis: Article 12 of Enterprise Law 59/2020/QH14.
Analysis: True. LLCs and joint-stock companies may have one or more legal representatives; the charter sets their number, titles, rights and duties. At least one must reside in Vietnam.
Note: With several representatives, the charter should define signing authority to avoid disputes over contract and voucher validity.

ACC-067.q: An LLC may distribute profits to members only after fulfilling tax and other financial obligations and ensuring it can pay all debts and obligations due after the distribution.
ACC-067.x:
Basis: Article 69 (multi-member LLC) and Article 76 (single-member LLC) of the 2020 Enterprise Law.
Analysis: True. Profits may be distributed only after tax and other financial obligations are met and the company can still pay debts falling due after distribution – a creditor-protection rule.
Note: Members receiving improper distributions must repay them; owners/members are jointly liable for unrepaid amounts.

ACC-068.q: A supplier payable of USD 100,000 was recognised at 25,000 VND/USD. At year-end, the bank's transfer selling rate is 26,000 VND/USD. What is the revaluation exchange loss (VND)?
ACC-068.x:
Basis: VAS 10; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (revaluation rates for monetary items).
Working: Foreign-currency payables use the bank's transfer selling rate: 100,000 × (26,000 − 25,000) = 100,000,000 VND. Liability rises → FX loss: Dr 413 / Cr 331, then Dr 635 / Cr 413.
Note: Receivables use the buying rate (ACC-103); payables use the selling rate.

ACC-069.q: Non-deductible input VAT is included in the asset's cost or the related expense (if it meets expense conditions).
ACC-069.e: True. For example, goods used for non-VAT activities.
ACC-069.x:
Basis: VAT Law 48/2024/QH15; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; VAS 02 and VAS 03.
Analysis: True. Non-creditable input VAT (for exempt activities, invoices failing conditions…) is a real cost, so it's added to fixed asset cost, inventory cost or the related period expense.
Note: For CIT deductibility the spend must still meet voucher and non-cash payment rules (from 5 million VND).

ACC-070.q: Monthly allocation of factory fire insurance prepaid for the whole year:
ACC-070.e: Account 242 under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC is named 'Deferred expenses awaiting allocation'.
ACC-070.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (account 242 – Deferred costs); VAS 01 (matching).
Analysis: On prepaying annual insurance: Dr 242 / Cr 112. Monthly, allocate the factory portion (production overheads): Dr 627 / Cr 242 – matching cost to the insured period.
Distractors: B reverses; C expenses from the bank though cash was paid earlier; D uses 335 (accruals), wrong since cash is already out.

ACC-071.q: Opening stock 1,000 kg at VND 20,000/kg; purchases 3,000 kg at VND 24,000/kg; issued 2,500 kg. Under FIFO, what is the value issued (VND)?
ACC-071.x:
Basis: VAS 02 – Inventories (FIFO).
Working: Issue 2,500 kg: all 1,000 kg opening × 20,000 = 20 million; plus 1,500 kg of the purchase × 24,000 = 36 million → 56,000,000 VND. Closing 1,500 kg × 24,000 = 36 million. Check: 56 + 36 = 92 million total.
Note: Weighted average gives 57.5 million (ACC-028); with rising prices FIFO yields lower cost and higher profit.

ACC-072.q: Select ALL common reconciling items in a bank reconciliation:
o: Deposits in transit (recorded by the enterprise, not yet by the bank)
Payment orders issued but not yet debited by the bank
Bank fees and interest not yet recorded by the enterprise
Recording errors by the enterprise or the bank
ACC-072.e: Credit sales do not affect the bank account.
ACC-072.x:
Basis: 2015 Accounting Law (reconciliation); Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (accounts 112, 113); VSA 500, 505.
Analysis: Common book-to-statement differences: (A) deposits in transit; (B) payment orders issued but not yet debited; (C) bank fees and interest not yet booked; (D) errors by either party.
Distractors: (E) Credit sales only raise account 131; no cash moves, so no bank difference.
Note: Old, unexplained reconciling items are fraud red flags (lapping, fictitious payments).

ACC-073.q: In consolidated financial statements, intra-group transactions and unrealised profits must be eliminated in full.
ACC-073.e: True. Sales between parent and subsidiaries do not create consolidated revenue or profit.
ACC-073.x:
Basis: VAS 25 – Consolidated FS; Circular 202/2014/TT-BTC (consolidation guidance).
Analysis: True. Consolidated FS present the group as one entity; intra-group balances and transactions (revenue, COGS, receivables/payables, dividends) and unrealised profits in inventory or fixed assets are eliminated in full. Unrealised losses are also eliminated unless cost isn't recoverable.
Note: See ACC-112 for a worked example.

ACC-074.q: Under VAS 18, a contingent liability (outflow not probable or not reliably measurable) is:
o: Disclosed in the notes, not recognised
ACC-074.e: Unless the possibility of outflow is remote, in which case no disclosure is needed.
ACC-074.x:
Basis: VAS 18 – Provisions, contingent liabilities and assets.
Analysis: Contingent liabilities (possible obligations, or present obligations not reliably measurable) aren't recognised; their nature and estimated effect are disclosed. If an outflow is remote, no disclosure is needed.
Distractors: B requires all 3 provision conditions (ACC-033); C has no basis; D is wrong as the information may be material.

ACC-075.q: Upgrade costs that increase capacity or extend the useful life of a fixed asset are capitalised; routine repair costs are expensed.
ACC-075.e: True. Distinguish capital expenditure from repairs.
ACC-075.x:
Basis: VAS 03 – Property, plant and equipment; Article 7 of Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Subsequent costs raising future benefits (capacity, useful life, product quality, lower operating cost) are capitalised; routine maintenance to keep assets running is expensed.
Note: Major repairs not adding capacity may be spread via account 242; misclassification affects both profit and tax.

ACC-076.q: A truck costing VND 500 million with accumulated depreciation of 400 million is sold for 150 million excluding VAT. What is the gain on disposal (VND)?
ACC-076.e: Net book value 100 million; gain = 150 − 100 = 50,000,000 VND (other income 711 less other expenses 811).
ACC-076.x:
Basis: VAS 03; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (accounts 711, 811).
Working: Carrying amount = 500 − 400 = 100 million. Other income (711) = 150 million; other expense (811) = 100 million. Gain = 150 − 100 = 50,000,000 VND.
Note: Output VAT on the price (Cr 3331) doesn't affect the gain; disposal costs (dismantling, brokerage) go to 811.

ACC-077.q: Derecognising a fixed asset on disposal (net book value to other expenses):
ACC-077.e: Also record disposal proceeds: Dr 112/131 / Cr 711, Cr 3331.
ACC-077.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Derecognising a disposed asset: Dr 214 (accumulated depreciation), Dr 811 (carrying amount) / Cr 211 (cost). Also record proceeds Dr 112/131 / Cr 711, Cr 3331.
Distractors: B reverses; C records depreciation without removing cost; D puts carrying amount in admin expense – disposal is an 'other' activity.

ACC-078.q: Match each Vietnamese accounting standard with its topic:
ACC-078.e: Standards frequently applied in manufacturing enterprises.
ACC-078.x:
Basis: The 26 Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Decisions 149/2001, 165/2002, 234/2003, 12/2005, 100/2005/QĐ-BTC).
Analysis: VAS 02 – Inventories; VAS 03 – PP&E; VAS 14 – Revenue and other income; VAS 17 – Income taxes; VAS 24 – Cash flow statement.
Note: Roughly IAS 2, IAS 16, IAS 18 (now IFRS 15), IAS 12, IAS 7 – useful for IFRS/VFRS conversion.

ACC-079.q: Advances to suppliers and advances from customers in foreign currency are non-monetary items and are not revalued at the closing rate.
ACC-079.e: True. Only monetary items (cash, receivables, payables settled in money) are revalued.
ACC-079.x:
Basis: VAS 10; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Monetary items are cash and items settled in fixed amounts of money. Advances to suppliers and from customers settle in goods/services, so they're non-monetary – kept at transaction-date rates, not revalued.
Note: If goods won't arrive and cash will be refunded, the advance becomes a monetary receivable.

ACC-080.q: The useful life and depreciation method of fixed assets should be reviewed periodically; changes are treated as changes in accounting estimates (prospective).
ACC-080.e: True. Changes require a decision and disclosure.
ACC-080.x:
Basis: VAS 03 (review of useful life and method); VAS 29; Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Useful life and depreciation method are reviewed periodically (usually year-end). Changes are estimate changes – prospective: the carrying amount is spread over the remaining life; prior years aren't restated.
Note: Circular 45/2013 requires a decision and justification; methods may change at most once for tax purposes.

ACC-081.q: Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC guiding the subjects, scope and manner of applying IFRS in Vietnam takes effect from:
ACC-081.e: Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC was issued on 18/8/2026 and takes effect on 01/01/2027.
ACC-081.x:
Basis: Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC (per the question's source).
Analysis: Issued 18/08/2026, effective 01/01/2027 – the start of the common financial year for consistent adoption.
Distractors: B is the issue date; C and D are wrong.
Note: This text post-dates the assistant's knowledge; the explanation follows the question's source – check the original on the Ministry of Finance portal.

ACC-082.q: Under Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC, an enterprise voluntarily applying IFRS must notify the MOF in writing at least 30 days before starting or stopping application.
ACC-082.e: True. Starting or stopping takes effect from the beginning of the next financial year.
ACC-082.x:
Basis: Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC (per the question's source).
Analysis: True. Voluntary IFRS adopters must notify the Ministry of Finance in writing at least 30 days before starting or stopping; the change takes effect from the next financial year – no mid-year framework switch.
Note: Check the original, as the circular post-dates the assistant's knowledge.

ACC-083.q: Under Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC, enterprises applying IFRS may modify the standards' content to suit their circumstances.
ACC-083.e: False. IFRS must be applied as issued, without modification, and consistently throughout the financial year.
ACC-083.x:
Basis: Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC (per the question's source); IAS 1 (statement of IFRS compliance).
Analysis: False. IFRS must be applied in full, unmodified, and consistently within the financial year. IAS 1 allows an 'IFRS compliant' statement only if every requirement is met – selective application destroys international comparability, IFRS's main purpose.

ACC-084.q: Under the plan announced by the MOF on 13/10/2026, how many Vietnamese Financial Reporting Standards (VFRS), based on IFRS, will the system comprise?
ACC-084.e: 42 VFRS based on IFRS 2026, in 3 phases (10 – 21 – 11 standards) until 2029; mandatory application expected from 01/01/2031.
ACC-084.x:
Basis: Ministry of Finance VFRS launch conference, 13/10/2026 (per the question's source).
Analysis: Plan: 42 VFRS based on IFRS 2026, in 3 phases (10 – 21 – 11 standards) to 2029; mandatory from 01/01/2031 expected. Check: 10 + 21 + 11 = 42.
Distractors: 26 is the current VAS count; 37 and 17 are wrong.
Note: It's a plan as announced and may change; it post-dates the assistant's knowledge.

ACC-085.q: Under the VFRS plan (10/2026), after completing the 42 standards, the MOF expects to issue a circular making them mandatory nationwide from 01/01/2031.
ACC-085.e: True. The motto is 'launch together, issue in sequence'; simpler standards come first.
ACC-085.x:
Basis: Ministry of Finance VFRS launch conference, 13/10/2026 (per the question's source).
Analysis: True. The approach is 'start together, issue in stages': simpler standards first (ACC-128); once all 42 are done, a circular is expected to mandate them nationwide from 01/01/2031.
Note: 2031 is indicative; businesses should prepare data early for big gaps (leases – IFRS 16, financial instruments – IFRS 9, revenue – IFRS 15).

ACC-086.q: Select ALL laws that amended Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13 (consolidated in Consolidated Text 41/VBHN-VPQH of 2026):
ACC-086.x:
Basis: Consolidated text 41/VBHN-VPQH (2026) of the Accounting Law (per the question's source).
Analysis: Three laws amended Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13: (A) Tax Administration Law 38/2019/QH14 (effective 01/07/2020); (B) Law 56/2024/QH15 amending the Securities, Accounting and Independent Audit Laws… (01/01/2025); (C) Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15 (01/07/2026).
Distractors: (D) the 2020 Enterprise Law didn't amend the Accounting Law.
Note: Cite the consolidated text to avoid missing amendments.

ACC-087.q: Under the Accounting Law, enterprise managers may not concurrently act as accountant, storekeeper or cashier (except sole proprietorships and single-member LLCs owned by an individual).
ACC-087.e: True. Article 13(7) of the Accounting Law — segregation of duties.
ACC-087.x:
Basis: Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13 (consolidated 2026) – Article 13(7) per the question's source; Article 52 on incompatible roles.
Analysis: True. Legal representatives, directors and managers may not also be accountants, storekeepers or cashiers – except sole proprietorships and single-individual-owner LLCs (small, owner bears the risk). Purpose: separate spending authority from recording and custody (COSO segregation of duties, ACC-003).

ACC-088.q: Under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC, a lactating dairy herd (livestock yielding periodic produce) is recorded in account:
ACC-088.e: Account 2151 – livestock yielding periodic produce; 2152 – livestock yielding produce once.
ACC-088.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (account 215 – Biological assets).
Analysis: Milking cows produce repeatedly → account 2151 – Animals producing periodically.
Distractors: B (211) is ordinary PP&E – Circular 99 separates biological assets; C (152) is raw materials; D (2152) is for one-off produce animals (beef cattle).

ACC-089.q: SMEs may still choose to apply the accounting regime under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC instead of the SME regime.
ACC-089.e: True. SMEs may choose the full regime if it suits their management needs.
ACC-089.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; Circular 133/2016/TT-BTC (SME accounting regime).
Analysis: True. SMEs may opt for the full regime under Circular 99/2025 (replacing Circular 200) if it suits management, investor or bank needs; once chosen it applies consistently for at least the financial year, with notice to the tax office.
Note: Firms planning fundraising, listing or IFRS should consider adopting the full regime early.

ACC-090.q: Inventory costs VND 800 million; estimated selling price 780 million; estimated costs to sell 30 million. What inventory write-down provision is required (VND million)?
ACC-090.x:
Basis: VAS 02; Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC.
Working: NRV = 780 − 30 = 750 million. Cost 800 > NRV 750 → allowance = 800 − 750 = 50 million VND (Dr 632 / Cr 2294 – ACC-091).
Common error: 20 million (comparing 780 to cost, forgetting selling costs).

ACC-091.q: The entry to record an inventory write-down provision is:
ACC-091.e: Inventory write-down provisions increase cost of goods sold.
ACC-091.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Inventory write-down allowance: Dr 632 (COGS) / Cr 2294. Reversal when NRV recovers: Dr 2294 / Cr 632.
Distractors: B is the reversal; C is the doubtful-debt allowance (ACC-056); D misuses financial expense and credits goods directly.

ACC-092.q: Machinery costing VND 960 million is put into use on 01/4/2026, depreciated straight-line over 8 years. What is the 2026 depreciation (VND million)?
ACC-092.e: Annual depreciation = 960/8 = 120; 9 months in 2026: 120 × 9/12 = 90 million VND.
ACC-092.x:
Basis: Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC (depreciation from the in-service date).
Working: Annual = 960 / 8 = 120 million (10 million/month). In service 01/04/2026 → 9 months in 2026 (Apr–Dec): 10 × 9 = 90 million VND.
Note: Circular 45 depreciates from the start-of-use date; 1 April gives exactly 9 months.

ACC-093.q: A truck is bought: price excluding VAT VND 900 million, deductible VAT 90 million, registration fee 18 million, registration and inspection 2 million. What is the fixed asset cost (VND million)?
ACC-093.x:
Basis: VAS 03; Article 4 of Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC.
Working: Cost = price (net of discounts) + non-refundable taxes + directly attributable costs = 900 + 18 (registration fee) + 2 (registration, inspection) = 920 million VND.
Common error: 1,010 million (adding the 90 million creditable VAT – that goes to Dr 1332, not cost).

ACC-094.q: Under VAS 06, a finance lease is one where the lessor:
ACC-094.e: Ownership may transfer at the end of the term; other leases are operating leases.
o: Transfers substantially all risks and rewards incidental to ownership to the lessee
ACC-094.x:
Basis: VAS 06 – Leases.
Analysis: A finance lease transfers substantially all risks and rewards of ownership to the lessee; title may or may not pass at the end. Indicators: title transfer, bargain purchase option, lease term covering most of the economic life, PV of payments near fair value.
Distractors: B describes an operating lease; C and D aren't classification criteria.

ACC-095.q: Unlike IFRS 16, under VAS 06 operating lessees expense rent on a straight-line basis and do not recognise a right-of-use asset in the statement of financial position.
ACC-095.e: True. This is a major difference when converting to IFRS/VFRS.
ACC-095.x:
Basis: VAS 06; IFRS 16.
Analysis: True. Under VAS 06, operating lessees expense rent straight-line with no asset or liability. IFRS 16 removes lessee classification: most leases (except short-term, low-value) bring a right-of-use asset and lease liability on balance sheet.
Note: On conversion, assets and liabilities rise and EBITDA rises (rent becomes depreciation + interest) – affecting leverage ratios and loan covenants.

ACC-096.q: Opening stock 500 kg at VND 30,000; on day 5, 1,500 kg purchased at VND 32,000; on day 10, 1,200 kg issued. Under FIFO, what is closing inventory (VND)?
ACC-096.x:
Basis: VAS 02 (FIFO).
Working: Available: 500 kg × 30,000 + 1,500 kg × 32,000 = 15 + 48 = 63 million (2,000 kg). FIFO issue of 1,200 kg: 500 × 30,000 + 700 × 32,000 = 15 + 22.4 = 37.4 million. Closing = 800 kg × 32,000 = 25,600,000 VND. Check: 37.4 + 25.6 = 63 million.
Note: Under FIFO, closing stock carries the latest purchase prices.

ACC-097.q: Match each VAS with its topic:
ACC-097.x:
Basis: The 26 Vietnamese Accounting Standards issued 2001–2005.
Analysis: VAS 04 – Intangible assets; VAS 06 – Leases; VAS 16 – Borrowing costs; VAS 18 – Provisions, contingent liabilities and assets; VAS 26 – Related party disclosures.
Note: Equivalent to IAS 38, IAS 17 (now IFRS 16), IAS 23, IAS 37, IAS 24.

ACC-098.q: Under VAS 21, enterprises may not offset assets and liabilities or income and expenses unless another standard requires or permits it.
ACC-098.e: True. The no-offsetting principle in financial statement presentation.
ACC-098.x:
Basis: VAS 21 – Presentation of financial statements.
Analysis: True. Assets and liabilities, income and expenses aren't offset unless another standard requires or permits it (e.g., net FX gains/losses, net disposal gains). Offsetting hides the scale of risk.
Note: A common error is netting receivables and payables with the same counterparty without a legal right of set-off.

ACC-099.q: An enterprise receives a VND 200 million advance from a customer for delivery next month. The entry on receipt is:
ACC-099.e: Customer advances are credited to account 131 (customer advances detail); revenue is recognised on delivery.
ACC-099.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (account 131 – customer advances); VAS 14.
Analysis: On receipt: Dr 112 / Cr 131. No revenue yet as risks and rewards haven't passed (ACC-025). On delivery: Dr 131 / Cr 511, Cr 3331. A credit balance on 131 is shown as 'Advances from customers' (a liability).
Distractors: B books revenue early; C has no cash; D – account 3387 (unearned revenue) is for multi-period receipts like rent, not purchase deposits.

ACC-100.q: Interest incurred to build a factory (18-month construction) during the investment phase is recorded as:
ACC-100.e: Under VAS 16, borrowing costs directly attributable to qualifying assets are capitalised into construction in progress.
ACC-100.x:
Basis: VAS 16 – Borrowing costs; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: An 18-month factory build is a qualifying asset (> 12 months) → interest during construction is capitalised: Dr 241 / Cr 335 (accrued) or Cr 112 (paid). Capitalisation stops when the asset is substantially complete; later interest goes to Dr 635.
Distractors: B expenses interest during the qualifying period; C and D misclassify.
Note: Capitalisation is suspended during abnormal interruptions.

ACC-101.q: An enterprise has accounting profit before tax of VND 1,200 million; current CIT expense 260 million; deferred tax expense 20 million. What is profit after tax (VND million)?
ACC-101.x:
Basis: VAS 17; income statement format under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Working: Total CIT expense = current 260 + deferred 20 = 280 million. Profit after tax = 1,200 − 280 = 920 million VND.
Note: Effective rate = 280/1,200 = 23.3% > 20% – implying non-deductible costs or temporary differences; reconcile in the notes.

ACC-102.e: Account 419 is renamed 'Own shares repurchased'; enterprises issue their own accounting regulations without MOF approval.
o: Account 242 is named 'Deferred expenses awaiting allocation'.
Enterprises must seek MOF approval to add accounts.
ACC-102.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True: account 242 – 'Deferred costs'; 112 – 'Demand deposits' (ACC-017). False: 419 is now 'Own shares repurchased'; businesses issue their own accounting rules and add accounts without Ministry approval (ACC-019).

ACC-103.q: A receivable of USD 50,000 was recognised at 25,300 VND/USD. At year-end, the bank's transfer buying rate is 25,900 VND/USD. What is the revaluation exchange gain (VND million)?
ACC-103.e: Receivables are revalued at the buying rate: 50,000 × (25,900 − 25,300) = 30 million VND, recorded as financial income.
ACC-103.x:
Basis: VAS 10; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Working: Receivables revalue at the transfer buying rate: 50,000 × (25,900 − 25,300) = 50,000 × 600 = 30,000,000 VND. Asset rises → FX gain: Dr 131 / Cr 413, then Dr 413 / Cr 515.
Note: Receivables use the buying rate, payables the selling rate (ACC-068) – reflecting settlement reality.

ACC-104.q: Under VAS 01, financial statements should reflect the economic substance of transactions rather than their legal form (within the standards).
ACC-104.e: True. Faithful, objective presentation of substance underlies accounting.
ACC-104.x:
Basis: VAS 01 (faithfulness, objectivity); VAS 21; 2015 Accounting Law.
Analysis: True. Accounting must reflect economic substance, not just legal form (within the standards). E.g., a 'sale and leaseback' that is really a loan; goods sent to agents aren't revenue though shipped.
Note: Key when reviewing complex or related-party transactions.

ACC-105.q: Under VAS 04, research-phase costs of an internal software project are:
ACC-105.e: Research costs are expensed immediately; only development-phase costs meeting all criteria are capitalised.
ACC-105.x:
Basis: VAS 04 – Intangible assets.
Analysis: Research-phase costs are expensed immediately since future benefits can't be shown. Only development-phase costs meeting all 6 conditions (ACC-106) are capitalised.
Distractors: B capitalises the wrong phase; C – spreading costs has no basis in the standard; D has no basis.

ACC-106.q: Select ALL conditions to capitalise development costs as an intangible asset under VAS 04:
ACC-106.e: Pre-orders are not a VAS 04 requirement (probable future economic benefits suffice).
o: Technical feasibility of completing the asset
Intention and ability to use or sell it
The asset will generate future economic benefits
Adequate resources to complete and reliably measurable costs
ACC-106.x:
Basis: VAS 04 – Intangible assets (development cost capitalisation).
Analysis: Conditions: (A) technical feasibility; (B) intent to complete and ability to use or sell; (C) probable future benefits; (D) adequate technical and financial resources and reliable cost measurement (plus ability to use/sell; meeting useful-life and value criteria).
Distractors: (E) Pre-orders aren't required – merely possible evidence for the benefits condition.

ACC-107.q: A receivable of VND 300 million is 2 years 3 months overdue, fully documented. What is the maximum provision under Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC (VND million)?
ACC-107.e: Overdue 2 to under 3 years: 70% × 300 = 210 million VND.
ACC-107.x:
Basis: Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC.
Working: 2 years 3 months overdue falls in 2 to under 3 years → up to 70%: 300 × 70% = 210 million VND (ACC-050).
Note: Full documentation (contract, confirmations, dunning) is required for CIT deductibility.

ACC-108.q: Electronic ledgers and documents must be secure, confidential and retrievable for the retention period under the Accounting Law.
ACC-108.e: True. Electronic storage must ensure integrity, retrievability and protection against unauthorised changes.
ACC-108.x:
Basis: Article 41 of Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13 (consolidated 2026); Decree 174/2016/ND-CP; 2023 E-Transactions Law.
Analysis: True. Electronic records must be stored securely with integrity, tamper protection and retrievability/printability throughout the retention period (5/10 years or permanent – ACC-001).
Note: Changing accounting software needs a migration plan with readable backups of old data.

ACC-109.q: Arrange the year-end closing and FS preparation workflow:
ACC-109.e: Closing flow: count – adjust – tax – close accounts – prepare statements.
o: Count cash, inventory, fixed assets; reconcile receivables/payables
Depreciate, allocate costs, make provisions, revalue foreign currency
Determine current and deferred CIT expense
Close revenue and expenses to account 911 and determine profit
Prepare the statement of financial position, income statement, cash flow statement and notes
ACC-109.x:
Basis: Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13 (Article 26 on closing); Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Order: (1) count cash, inventory, fixed assets, confirm balances – establishing actual figures; (2) period-end adjustments (depreciation, amortisation, allowances, FX revaluation); (3) current and deferred CIT – needing adjusted profit; (4) close to 911 and determine profit; (5) prepare the FS.
Note: Computing tax before adjustments misstates tax; reporting before closing misstates profit.

ACC-110.q: Under VAS 07, investments in associates in consolidated financial statements are accounted for using:
ACC-110.e: The equity method in consolidated FS; the cost method in separate FS.
o: Fair value through profit or loss
ACC-110.x:
Basis: VAS 07 – Investments in associates.
Analysis: Associates (significant influence, usually 20% to under 50% of votes): equity method in consolidated FS (cost adjusted for the investor's share of profit/loss); cost method in separate FS.
Distractors: B is for separate FS; C is for subsidiaries (VAS 25); D isn't used under VAS.

ACC-111.q: Control is presumed when the parent directly or indirectly holds more than 50% of the subsidiary's voting rights.
ACC-111.e: True under VAS 25, unless it can be clearly shown that control does not exist.
ACC-111.x:
Basis: VAS 25.
Analysis: True. Control is presumed when the parent holds, directly or through subsidiaries, over 50% of votes, unless clearly shown otherwise. Control can also exist below 50% (agreements with other investors, power to appoint most of the board, power over policies).

ACC-112.q: A parent sells goods to its subsidiary for VND 500 million at a cost of 400 million. At year-end, the subsidiary still holds 40% of the goods. What unrealised profit must be eliminated on consolidation (VND million)?
ACC-112.e: Intra-group profit = 500 − 400 = 100; 40% remaining in inventory → 40 million VND to eliminate.
ACC-112.x:
Basis: VAS 25; Circular 202/2014/TT-BTC.
Working: Intra-group margin = 500 − 400 = 100 million (20% of sales). 40% remains in the subsidiary's stock → unrealised profit = 100 × 40% = 40 million VND. Consolidation entry: reduce revenue 500, COGS 460, inventory 40.
Note: A deferred tax asset may arise on the eliminated unrealised profit.

ACC-113.q: Under Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC, enterprises adopting IFRS for the first time must follow the transition and presentation requirements of IFRS 1.
ACC-113.e: True. IFRS 1 governs the opening statement of financial position and exemptions.
ACC-113.x:
Basis: Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC (per the question's source); IFRS 1 – First-time adoption.
Analysis: True. First-time adopters follow IFRS 1: an opening IFRS statement of financial position, retrospective IFRS policies (subject to exemptions and mandatory exceptions), and reconciliations of equity and profit from the old framework.
Note: Circular 118 post-dates the assistant's knowledge; IFRS 1 itself is stable.

ACC-114.q: Annual financial statements must be published within (for enterprises not subject to mandatory audit):
ACC-114.e: Article 31 of the Accounting Law: publish within 120 days; entities subject to audit publish with the audit report.
o: 120 days after the end of the annual accounting period
ACC-114.x:
Basis: Article 31 of Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13.
Analysis: Annual FS must be published within 120 days of year-end; mandatory-audit entities publish with the audit report. Public and listed companies face shorter securities deadlines.
Distractors: 30, 60 and 180 days are wrong.
Note: Distinguish from the 90-day filing deadline (ACC-011).

ACC-115.q: Under VAS 15, construction contract revenue (when the outcome can be estimated reliably) is recognised by stage of completion.
ACC-115.e: True. Revenue and costs follow the stage of completion or customer-certified work value.
ACC-115.x:
Basis: VAS 15 – Construction contracts.
Analysis: True. With reliable estimates: under progress billing, recognise by stage of completion determined by the contractor; under billing by work performed, recognise per customer-certified volume. Expected losses are recognised immediately.
Note: Without reliable estimates, revenue is limited to recoverable costs incurred.

ACC-116.q: A construction contract has total revenue of VND 10 billion and estimated total costs of 8 billion. Actual costs to year-end are 3.2 billion. Under the cost-to-cost method, what revenue is recognised this year (VND billion)?
ACC-116.e: Stage of completion = 3.2/8 = 40%; revenue = 40% × 10 = 4 billion VND.
ACC-116.x:
Basis: VAS 15 (cost-to-cost method).
Working: Stage of completion = actual cumulative cost / total estimated cost = 3.2 / 8 = 40%. Revenue = 40% × 10 = 4 billion VND; cost 3.2 billion → gross profit 0.8 billion (20%, matching the 2/10 expected margin).
Note: Materials bought but not yet used aren't included in the stage of completion.

ACC-117.q: Settlement (cash) discounts received for paying suppliers early are recognised as:
ACC-117.e: Discounts received are financial income; discounts given to customers are financial expenses (635).
o: A reduction of cost of goods sold
ACC-117.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (accounts 515, 635).
Analysis: Settlement discounts (for early payment) are financial – time value of money – so discounts received: Dr 331 / Cr 515; discounts given: Dr 635 / Cr 131.
Distractors: B and C confuse it with trade discounts (lower purchase cost); D misclassifies.

ACC-118.q: Trade discounts granted to customers (not shown on the invoice) are recorded as revenue deductions.
ACC-118.e: True. Trade discounts, price reductions and sales returns are revenue deductions (account 521).
ACC-118.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (account 521); VAS 14.
Analysis: True. Trade discounts, allowances and returns arising after revenue is booked go to account 521 – revenue deductions – closed against 511 to arrive at net revenue.
Note: If the trade discount is deducted on the invoice, revenue is booked net, bypassing 521.

ACC-119.q: Select ALL mandatory related party disclosures under VAS 26:
ACC-119.e: Related party disclosures focus on relationships, nature, amounts and pricing policies.
o: Trade names of products sold to independent customers
ACC-119.x:
Basis: VAS 26 – Related party disclosures.
Analysis: Required: (A) relationships with controlling parties (even with no transactions); (B) nature of transactions; (C) amounts and closing balances; (D) pricing policy.
Distractors: (E) Brand names sold to independent customers are irrelevant.
Note: These disclosures also feed tax transfer-pricing files (Decree 132/2020).

ACC-120.q: In 2026 the MOF allowed members of the International Financial Centre in Vietnam to apply full IFRS under Resolution 222/2025/QH15 and Decree 325/2025/ND-CP.
ACC-120.e: True. Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC lets these enterprises continue if their financial policies do not change.
ACC-120.x:
Basis: Resolution 222/2025/QH15 on the International Financial Centre; Decree 325/2025/ND-CP; Circular 118/2026/TT-BTC (per the question's source).
Analysis: True. Members of Vietnam's International Financial Centre may apply full IFRS under Resolution 222; Circular 118 lets them continue if financial policies are unchanged.
Note: These texts post-date the assistant's knowledge; the explanation follows the question's source.

ACC-121.q: A raw material shortage of VND 20 million is unexplained; after resolution, the storekeeper compensates 60% and the rest goes to cost of sales. How much is charged to cost of sales (VND million)?
ACC-121.e: 20 × 40% = 8 million VND (Dr 632); 12 million compensated by the storekeeper (Dr 1388/334).
ACC-121.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (accounts 1381, 1388, 632).
Working: On discovering an unexplained shortage: Dr 1381 / Cr 152 – 20 million. After resolution: storekeeper pays 60% = 12 million (Dr 1388 or 334 / Cr 1381); remaining 40% = 8 million to Dr 632 / Cr 1381.
Note: Abnormal losses hit COGS but aren't CIT-deductible without records on cause and responsibility.

ACC-122.q: Under VAS 05, investment property leased out is presented at cost less accumulated depreciation; investment property held for capital appreciation is not depreciated but tested for impairment.
ACC-122.e: True under current guidance; unlike IFRS (IAS 40), which permits a fair value model.
ACC-122.x:
Basis: VAS 05 – Investment property; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; IAS 40.
Analysis: True. Investment property held for operating leases is carried at cost less depreciation; property held for capital appreciation isn't depreciated but tested for impairment. IAS 40 allows cost or fair value models (fair value changes through profit or loss).
Note: This gap matters greatly for real estate firms converting to IFRS.

ACC-123.q: October salaries payable for the sales department are VND 80 million. The entry is:
ACC-123.e: Sales staff salaries go to account 641; direct production workers to 622.
ACC-123.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Sales staff wages: Dr 641 (selling expense) / Cr 334. Classify by department: production workers – 622; factory management – 627; sales – 641; administration – 642.
Distractors: B reverses; C uses the wrong department and account (338 is payroll contributions); D is direct production labour.

ACC-124.q: VAS 01 – Framework defines the elements of financial statements as assets, liabilities, equity, revenue/other income and expenses.
ACC-124.e: True. The five basic elements of financial statements.
ACC-124.x:
Basis: VAS 01 – Framework.
Analysis: True. Five FS elements: financial position – assets, liabilities, equity; performance – revenue and other income, expenses. Accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity; profit = income − expenses.

ACC-125.q: Dairy cows (biological assets) are bought at VND 60 million each, 50 cows; transport and quarantine cost 30 million for the herd. What cost is recognised in account 2151 (VND million)?
ACC-125.e: 50 × 60 + 30 = 3,030 million VND (purchase price plus directly attributable costs).
ACC-125.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (account 2151); VAS 02/VAS 03 (cost principle).
Working: Cost = purchase price + direct costs to bring the asset to use = 50 × 60 + 30 = 3,000 + 30 = 3,030 million VND (60.6 million per head).
Note: Creditable input VAT is excluded; care costs after the herd enters production are period production costs.

ACC-126.q: A chief accountant of an enterprise may not be:
ACC-126.e: Article 19 of Decree 174/2016/ND-CP lists persons who may not serve as chief accountant to ensure independence.
o: A parent, spouse, child or sibling of the legal representative, director or finance manager (except exempt entity types)
A holder of an accountant certificate
Someone with 5 years of accounting experience
ACC-126.x:
Basis: Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13; Article 19 of Decree 174/2016/ND-CP.
Analysis: Barred from being chief accountant: parents, spouses, children and siblings of the legal representative, head, director, deputy director in charge of finance, storekeeper or cashier (with exemptions such as sole proprietorships and individual-owned single-member LLCs). Purpose: independence of financial control.
Distractors: B, C and D are qualifications or experience – not barred persons.

ACC-127.q: Tools worth VND 24 million (below fixed-asset criteria) are allocated evenly over 2 years. What is the monthly allocation (VND)?
ACC-127.x:
Basis: Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC (items under 30 million aren't fixed assets; up to 3-year allocation); Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (account 242).
Working: 24,000,000 / (2 years × 12) = 24,000,000 / 24 = 1,000,000 VND/month. Entries: on issue Dr 242 / Cr 153; monthly Dr 627/641/642 / Cr 242.
Note: 2 years is within the 3-year maximum (ACC-045).

ACC-128.q: Under the VFRS plan, the first batch prioritises less complex standards such as segment reporting, cash flow statements, related parties and interim reporting.
ACC-128.x:
Basis: Ministry of Finance VFRS launch conference, 13/10/2026 (per the question's source).
Analysis: True. Phase 1 (2026–2027) has 10 simpler standards – segments, cash flows, related parties, interim reporting… – building on existing VAS (VAS 24, 26, 27, 28), easing firms in before harder ones (financial instruments, leases, revenue).
Note: This post-dates the assistant's knowledge; the explanation follows the question's source.

ACC-129.q: Under VAS 30, basic earnings per share equals:
ACC-129.e: Basic EPS uses the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding.
o: Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders / weighted average ordinary shares outstanding
ACC-129.x:
Basis: VAS 30 – Earnings per share; Circular 21/2006/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Basic EPS = profit (loss) attributable to ordinary shareholders (after preference dividends and bonus/welfare funds if any) / weighted average ordinary shares outstanding.
Distractors: B (PAT/charter capital) is a return-on-capital measure; C uses revenue and year-end shares; D is dividend over par.

ACC-130.q: At the start of the year there are 10 million ordinary shares; on 01/7, 2 million more are issued for cash. Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders is VND 22 billion. What is basic EPS (VND per share)?
ACC-130.e: Weighted shares = 10 + 2 × 6/12 = 11 million; EPS = 22,000 million / 11 million = 2,000 VND.
ACC-130.x:
Basis: VAS 30.
Working: Weighted shares = 10 million × 12/12 + 2 million × 6/12 = 10 + 1 = 11 million. EPS = 22,000 million / 11 million = 2,000 VND/share.
Note: Using 12 million year-end shares gives 1,833 – wrong. Bonus issues and splits are adjusted retrospectively as if outstanding all period, not time-weighted.
